title: Oncall Succession: dashboard prototype & metric sunset storyboard
body:
Purpose:
This working storyboard sketches a compact dashboard and metric-sunset workflow to make oncall succession less error-prone. Goal is to give the next-shift engineer a short, prioritized view (2–3 panels) that tells them whether to escalate, roll back, or monitor, and which signals can be retired from fast-changing experiments.

Context / motivation:
- Observability surface has grown fast over Q3–Q4 and many ephemeral signals remain in high-visibility dashboards. New oncall engineers are spending too long triaging low-value noise.
- We need a middle path: preserve high-fidelity anchors for immediate action while flagging candidates for deprecation and moving them to an experimentation playground.
- This doc sits between metric governance and dashboard UX: it pairs signal definitions with a concise visual storyboard for handoff.

Success criteria (how we'll measure this prototype):
- Median time-to-decision (first 3 actions: escalate / monitor / rollback) during handoff <= 6 minutes for new oncall in first 24h.
- Reduce dashboard panel count by 18% for the primary oncall view within one quarter.
- At least 6 low-value metrics identified and scheduled for deprecation or archive.

Storyboard overview (3-step oncall succession flow):
1) Alert summary card (top-left)
   - What it shows: active alerts sorted by severity + top suspected service/component.
   - Primary SLI snapshot: 1m p99 latency, error-rate (5m), token-serving throughput (1m).
   - Quick actions: accept, escalate, silence for N minutes.

2) Root-cause leash (middle)
   - Purpose: a compact set of correlating metrics and one anchored trace.
   - Metrics included: model-inference-latency-by-route, kvcache-hit-rate, host-gpu-load, queue-depth-by-pool.
   - Trace anchoring: a single sampled trace anchored to the alert's request-id/session-id with span breadcrumbs: auth -> routing -> model-invoke -> postprocess.

3) Operator guidance & deprecation note (right)
   - Shows: known mitigations (can restart pod, shift traffic to dedicated pool), recent rollout flag, last rollback time.
   - Deprecation flag: if metric flagged for deprecation, show reason and next-review date.

Metric definition template (for panels in the storyboard):
- name: short metric id (string)
- owner: pager/owner alias (who to page if escalated)
- description: what it measures and why it matters to oncall decisions
- alert-mapping: which alert groups this feeds and thresholds used
- sampling: recommended sampling rate or aggregation window for cost control
- retention-tier: hot | warm | archived (guides retention and query cost)

Example metric entries (compact):
- metric id: model-inference-latency-by-route
  owner: eng-serving-runtime-oncall
  description: 1m p99 of end-to-end token-generation latency partitioned by route tag. Used to detect high-latency or KV-cache misses.
  alert-mapping: p99 > 1200ms for 3 windows -> P1 alert
  sampling: full aggregation at 1m, traces sampled 1/1000 for post-hoc
  retention-tier: hot

- metric id: kvcache-hit-rate
  owner: eng-serving-runtime
  description: ratio of key-value cache hits over total lookups. Low hit rate correlates with cold starts and cost.
  alert-mapping: drop > 15% relative to baseline for 10m -> P2 alert
  sampling: aggregate 1m and 5m, sample raw keys for 1/10000 to protect cardinality
  retention-tier: warm

Trace anchoring rules (practical heuristics):
- Always include request-id or session-id in alert context. If missing, synthesize a session key for trace lookup.
- Prefer a single representative trace in the storyboard. Representative trace = highest token count request that matches the alert window and route tag.
- Include a short span map in UI: show span names, durations, and an estimated token-cost contribution.
- If trace contains PII/PHI, redact at pattern-level before allowing quick-linking in the oncall panel.

Dashboard wireframe notes (practical constraints):
- Keep top row to 3 panels (alert summary, rc leash, operator guidance) to fit common laptop sizes without scrolling.
- Each panel must have one-line provenance: who owns the metric, last update, linked jira/confluence.
- Small footprint widgets should make heavy use of sparklines + last-value badges rather than full time-series until expanded.
- Expand action: one-click deep-dive opens a sandboxed query page with suggested queries and relevant traces pre-filtered.

Ownership & lifecycle workflow (how metrics move toward deprecation):
- Triage window (14 days): metrics flagged as low-actionability enter triage. Owner documents use-cases.
- Experimentation window (30 days): recommended to move metric into an "experiment" dashboard namespace, reduce hot retention to warm, and disable alerts.
- Sunset decision: after experiment window, product/metrics council votes to archive or reinstate. Archive moves metric to queryable cold tier with 90d retention.

Operational play (oncall playbook snippets):
- When an alert spikes and model-inference-latency-by-route is high but kvcache-hit-rate is unchanged: suspect autoscaling/queueing; check queue-depth-by-pool and GPU-backed pool health.
- If trace shows long postprocess spans but server-side times small: investigate downstream connectors and network egress.
- If metric suspected for deprecation: add deprecation-flag to metric definition, set next-review date, and mute panel for 7 days to observe noise reduction.

Backlog items (practical next steps):
- Build a compact prototype template in the dashboard repo and link to JIRA-OBS-2142.
- Implement trace-anchor API to fetch representative trace by request-id (owned by eng-observability).
- Run a 6-week pilot with two oncall rotations and gather time-to-decision telemetry.
- Create a metric-sunset rubric and schedule first archive pass.

Open questions / discussion points:
- What is the acceptable level of panel compression before operators lose context? (tradeoff study needed)
- How to automate selection of representative trace without amplifying sampling costs?
- Should the deprecation workflow include a public list for cross-team objections?

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Draft the small prototype and circulate to Priya and Liam for UX feedback by 2026-02-25.
- Prepare a short playbook card for rotation handoff that references this storyboard.
- Add a simple query cost estimate for each candidate metric before pilot.

End of working storyboard.

(Internal working doc: expect shorthand, placeholders, and action items. Not final.)
